subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change private-LAN reachability semantics for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the missing diagnostic, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a product and security-boundary choice that automation should not make.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping broader private-network access policy in the related security trackers.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent parity as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep this behavior under the existing private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping broader private-network access policy in the related security trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: The central exec runtime and routing history most consistently routes through this owner signal.
